newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end at 7-year peak, gain 0.55 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end at 7-year peak, gain 0.55 pct.

text.p: Taiwan share prices flirted with the 10,000 point threshold on Monday but failed to pierce it, yet still finished at a seven-year peak in balanced trading that brokers said boded well for the market's future.

The weighted index rose to 9,995.37 points in early trade, but could not muster enough momentum for a final push above 10,000 and settled for a 9,923.05 finish -- a gain of 0.55 percent or 53.80 points.
The close was still the market's highest since it posted 9,978.86 on April 12, 1990.
Turnover was relatively heavy at T$192 billion.

Taiwan's stock market bulls, charging for more than a year, picked up the pace in June and July, pushing the index up by 21 percent since June 1 on expectations of a gathering recovery spearheaded by the high-technology electronic industry.

At 10,000 points, the index would be a dramatic 113 percent above the 4,692.40 political nadir of March 12, 1996, when China was menacing the island with war games and unarmed missile tests in a drive to cool any ambitions for Taiwan independence. A close at 10,000 would mean a 47 percent rise in 1997 alone.
The closely watched electronics sector, which sagged in early trade, pulled off a late reversal to rise with most other sectors and had gained 0.74 percent by the close.
Plastics gained 1.3 percent, constructions rose 0.7 percent and the heavily weighted financials edged up 0.15 percent.
Analysts hailed the across-the-board rise. "The gains were evenly spread, which is good for the market's future," said Lin Long-hsien, senior analyst for United Securities.
"Unlike earlier in July, the market now no longer depends exclusively on electronics to push it higher," Lin said.
